title: REQ · Lock held and per-attempt timeout are proven by unit tests
summary: A held lock blocks Run without side effects and each attempt gets its own timeout
description: Context: Run takes lock.Acquire(LockPath) and runAttempt wraps each attempt in context.WithTimeout. Desired behavior: when the lock is held Run fails with lock.ErrLocked leaving the foreign lock file and the store untouched; with retries each attempt times out independently. Why: only one execution per World and bounded run time.
acceptance_criteria: Given the lock file exists, When Run is called, Then the lock file still exists afterwards and no execution record is stored
Given a blocking agent, Timeout 20ms and MaxRetries 1, When Run is called, Then the agent ran twice and the error wraps context.DeadlineExceeded

in_scope: Lock and timeout behavior of Runner.Run
